data.narrative:
NextSilicon is a Series B-stage AI & Software company founded by Elad Raz that has raised $200M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of four same-sector, same-stage private companies (Scale AI, Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, Field AI) alongside one public peer (Palantir), supplemented by eight additional private references.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $200M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $380M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of the four core comparables at $4.4B, with a range spanning $2.0B (Field AI) to $29.0B (Scale AI). Synthesizing these two approaches—weighted toward the peer-median given the robustness of same-stage comps—produces a triangulated range of $323M (conservative) to $5.1B (expansive), with a median point estimate of $2.4B.

Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion within the peer set, particularly Scale AI's outsized $29.0B valuation, which reflects market heterogeneity in AI & Software and raises questions about NextSilicon's relative competitive positioning and revenue trajectory. The stage-progression method's reliance on raised capital rather than revenue or profitability introduces additional noise. A valuation toward the lower-to-median range ($323M – $2.4B) appears more defensible absent evidence of Scale AI-tier market capture or pricing power.
